notes: Pass 29 independent artifact, generated 2026-08-24 at commit 835165dfcaba on a shared 2-vCPU sandbox (Intel Xeon @ 2.60GHz, Linux 6.1.158+). NOT robot hardware, NOT CPU-pinned, and NOT an official rustc build: no cargo/rustup/crates.io is reachable in this sandbox, so the binary was produced by mrustc against a from-source Rust 1.90.0 stdlib (GCC 12.2 C backend). THIS RUN: 3,335,788 msg/s, mean 156.52 us, p50 149.41 us, p99 353.51 us, max 375.20 us, 100000/100000 sent/received, message_size 64 B. WHAT THIS NUMBER IS: the harness measures CROSS-THREAD end-to-end latency between a producer and a consumer that spin-contend for 2 shared vCPUs, so the mean is dominated by thread scheduling, not by the ring buffer. Repeated runs on this machine gave means of 156.52 and 234.71 us for identical arguments - roughly 1.5x run-to-run spread - and Pass 27's artifact on a comparable sandbox measured 588.21 us. Treat the absolute value as environment-bound. WHAT THE RING ITSELF COSTS: tools/offline-mrustc/probes/microbench.rs, same machine, same commit, measures same-thread SPSC publish+consume at 110.90 ns/op (9.02M msg/s, 64 B payload, cap 1024), independently reproducing Pass 27's 112 ns/op. That is the figure that characterises the IPC path. CONCLUSION ON THE PUBLISHED CLAIMS: README's '6.2 us mean / 780K msg/s' and COMPARISON.md's '46x faster' are NOT supported by any executed measurement in this repository. Every real run of this harness has produced a cross-thread mean one to two orders of magnitude above 6.2 us, and benchmarks/results.json states in its own text that it is a TEMPLATE carrying those unverified figures. Also corrected: message_size is 64 B (canonical nros_types::Twist, repr(C)), not the template's 56. PROVENANCE OF THIS ARTIFACT: produced after the F29-09 fix. Before that fix the bench binary hung on 2/12 runs at 2000 iterations and 1/3 runs at 100000 (consumer exit condition unreachable), which is why the CI 'benchmarks' job has never reached a completed state.
